title: Weakness: no meal logged, so the alert waits for the rise
description: Glucose rises with no logged meal. Risk stays below the 35% alert threshold until the rise has begun: the alert fires at 14:50 (glucose 93 mg/dL, up from 70 at 14:35), 45 min before glucose first exceeds 180 mg/dL (15:35). With a logged meal (first scenario) the warning comes earlier. Stepping in 1-hour jumps skips the alert (14:45: 31%); the risk-history panel still shows it. What-ifs are recorded at 13:45 only.

primary.label: vs a zero-carb meal at the same time (isolates the carb content)

secondary.label: vs no meal (also includes the model's learned meal-timing expectation)

notes: Meals under 30 g are unreliable in this model: few training meals are that small and the audited small-meal differences are unstable.

joint_support.caveat: Training-support check: it flags meal inputs with no comparable example in the training data. It is not evidence that the forecast is wrong, and inputs inside the training range do not make a forecast accurate.

outside_tested_reasons: meal size outside the tested 20-120 g
twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. Fitted on synthetic training patients, selected on validation patients and tested once on held-out synthetic patients against simulator ground truth; the simulator's near-linear meal response favours it. The walk effect is cohort level (the twin has no personal activity parameter) and reflects the simulator's built-in exercise model. Not evidence about real patients; not advice.

result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.

joint_support.caveat: Training-support check: it flags meal inputs with no comparable example in the training data. It is not evidence that the forecast is wrong, and inputs inside the training range do not make a forecast accurate.

twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. Fitted on synthetic training patients, selected on validation patients and tested once on held-out synthetic patients against simulator ground truth; the simulator's near-linear meal response favours it. The walk effect is cohort level (the twin has no personal activity parameter) and reflects the simulator's built-in exercise model. Not evidence about real patients; not advice.

result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.

twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. reference.disclaimer: Research prototype on synthetic data. Not a medical device. Forecasts are not diagnoses or treatment instructions.

scenario.disclaimer: Research prototype on synthetic data. Not a medical device. Forecasts are not diagnoses or treatment instructions.

primary.label: vs a zero-carb meal at the same time (isolates the carb content)

secondary.label: vs no meal (also includes the model's learned meal-timing expectation)

notes: Logging any meal now (even zero-carb) shifts the +60-min forecast by +10.2 mg/dL and the risk by -19 points on its own: a learned meal-timing association, not physiology. That is why the no-meal comparison differs.

joint_support.caveat: Training-support check: it flags meal inputs with no comparable example in the training data. It is not evidence that the forecast is wrong, and inputs inside the training range do not make a forecast accurate.

twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. Fitted on synthetic training patients, selected on validation patients and tested once on held-out synthetic patients against simulator ground truth; the simulator's near-linear meal response favours it. The walk effect is cohort level (the twin has no personal activity parameter) and reflects the simulator's built-in exercise model. Not evidence about real patients; not advice.

result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.

joint_support.caveat: Training-support check: it flags meal inputs with no comparable example in the training data. It is not evidence that the forecast is wrong, and inputs inside the training range do not make a forecast accurate.

twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. Fitted on synthetic training patients, selected on validation patients and tested once on held-out synthetic patients against simulator ground truth; the simulator's near-linear meal response favours it. The walk effect is cohort level (the twin has no personal activity parameter) and reflects the simulator's built-in exercise model. Not evidence about real patients; not advice.

result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.

twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.

twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.

excursion.event_definition: Onset of a hyperglycaemic excursion (>= 3 consecutive CGM readings > 180 mg/dL, i.e. >= 15 min) within the next 120 min, predicted at times when the latest reading is <= 180 mg/dL.

scenario.disclaimer: Research prototype on synthetic data. Not a medical device. Forecasts are not diagnoses or treatment instructions.

primary.label: vs a zero-carb meal at the same time (isolates the carb content)

secondary.label: vs no meal (also includes the model's learned meal-timing expectation)

notes: Meals under 30 g are unreliable in this model: few training meals are that small and the audited small-meal differences are unstable.
Logging any meal now (even zero-carb) shifts the +60-min forecast by +13.5 mg/dL on its own: a learned meal-timing association, not physiology. That is why the no-meal comparison differs.

joint_support.caveat: Training-support check: it flags meal inputs with no comparable example in the training data. It is not evidence that the forecast is wrong, and inputs inside the training range do not make a forecast accurate.

twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. Fitted on synthetic training patients, selected on validation patients and tested once on held-out synthetic patients against simulator ground truth; the simulator's near-linear meal response favours it. The walk effect is cohort level (the twin has no personal activity parameter) and reflects the simulator's built-in exercise model. Not evidence about real patients; not advice.

result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.

twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.

excursion.event_definition: Onset of a hyperglycaemic excursion (>= 3 consecutive CGM readings > 180 mg/dL, i.e. >= 15 min) within the next 120 min, predicted at times when the latest reading is <= 180 mg/dL.

scenario.disclaimer: Research prototype on synthetic data. Not a medical device. Forecasts are not diagnoses or treatment instructions.

primary.label: vs a zero-carb meal at the same time (isolates the carb content)

secondary.label: vs no meal (also includes the model's learned meal-timing expectation)

notes: Meals under 30 g are unreliable in this model: few training meals are that small and the audited small-meal differences are unstable.

Logging any meal now (even zero-carb) shifts the +60-min forecast by +10.0 mg/dL and the risk by -6 points on its own: a learned meal-timing association, not physiology. That is why the no-meal comparison differs.

joint_support.caveat: Training-support check: it flags meal inputs with no comparable example in the training data. It is not evidence that the forecast is wrong, and inputs inside the training range do not make a forecast accurate.

twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. Fitted on synthetic training patients, selected on validation patients and tested once on held-out synthetic patients against simulator ground truth; the simulator's near-linear meal response favours it. The walk effect is cohort level (the twin has no personal activity parameter) and reflects the simulator's built-in exercise model. Not evidence about real patients; not advice.

result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.

notes: Logging any meal now (even zero-carb) shifts the +60-min forecast by +10.0 mg/dL and the risk by -6 points on its own: a learned meal-timing association, not physiology. That is why the no-meal comparison differs.

joint_support.caveat: Training-support check: it flags meal inputs with no comparable example in the training data. It is not evidence that the forecast is wrong, and inputs inside the training range do not make a forecast accurate.

twin_curve.caveat: Research estimate, not the served forecast. Fitted on synthetic training patients, selected on validation patients and tested once on held-out synthetic patients against simulator ground truth; the simulator's near-linear meal response favours it. The walk effect is cohort level (the twin has no personal activity parameter) and reflects the simulator's built-in exercise model. Not evidence about real patients; not advice.

result.disclaimer: Simulated what-if scenario. The hypothetical meal was never added to the patient record. Differences are learned associations of the forecasting models, not causal physiological effects. Not medical advice and not a treatment recommendation.
